pillars: Built with Cocoa for macOS, not a web page in a wrapper. Run, debug, IntelliSense, SQL, GitHub and AI are built in: no marketplace to search and no extensions to keep updated.
AI that works on your project
It is part of the editor so it can see your file, your selection, your project's instructions and the output of its commands. No copying back and forth between a chat window and your code.

why.title: Why jplus2: a native Mac editor with no extensions
why.text: Most editors start empty and ask you to assemble the rest. jplus2 starts complete, and it is made for the Mac and nothing else.

items.title: Truly native
items.text: Built with Cocoa for macOS, not a web page inside a wrapper. It starts fast, behaves like the rest of your Mac, and the whole app is a download of about 10 MB.

items.title: Complete from the first launch
items.text: Run, debug, IntelliSense, SQL, GitHub and AI are part of the app. There is no marketplace to search and no extensions to choose, set up and keep updated.

items.title: Databricks and Snowflake, one query away
items.text: Connect to Databricks on Azure, AWS or GCP and to Snowflake, and run SQL from the same window as your code. Also Azure SQL, Synapse, Azure SQL, Synapse, PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. Add GitHub and an AI agent in the same window, with no extensions to install.

items.title: AI on your terms
items.text: Connect your own Claude API key, any OpenAI-compatible service, or a model running on your Mac. jplus2 has no subscription, and your code is sent only when you ask.

items.title: Private by design
items.text: No account, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking. Passwords, tokens and API keys are kept in the macOS Keychain.

items.title: At home on your Mac
items.text: Liquid Glass on macOS 26, SF Symbols and SF Mono. The appearance follows macOS, or stays Light or Dark if you prefer. One app for Apple silicon and Intel.

features.title: Run, debug, SQL, GitHub and AI in one window

items.title: An assistant that sees what you see, and can work for you.
items.text: Ask a question and the assistant reads the file in front of you and your selection. Turn on Agent mode and it can also look around your project, propose file changes and propose terminal commands, one step at a time, and you approve each one.
bullets: Agent mode: reads files, shows every change as a diff to Apply or Cancel, and shows every command in the Terminal panel with Run and Reject; the output goes back to the assistant

Reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules from your project and keeps per-project memories. Type @ to bring in files, open tabs (even unsaved), line ranges, terminals, the diff, the branch or an earlier conversation
Reviews uncommitted changes or pull requests, and runs your own prompts from ai-commands.json
Claude with your own API key, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (including a local model such as Ollama), or a company gateway
Saves your conversations: reopen, search and export them as Markdown. Switch between Claude models from a menu under the chat
Inline suggestions (off by default): the next lines appear as grey text while you type. Tab accepts them, Option-Right takes one word, Escape drops them
MCP servers: connect the agent to tool servers over HTTP, and every call asks for your approval first
Full version only: none of this is in jplus2 Lite
items.alt: The assistant panel beside the editor, explaining a bug in the selected function.

items.title: An editor that keeps up with you.
items.text: The editing engine is Scintilla, known for its speed with large files. Around it, jplus2 adds the tools you use all day.
bullets: Syntax colouring and code folding for 95 languages
Multiple cursors, column editing, macros and bookmarks
Find, replace and mark with regular expressions, across all open files
A file explorer that follows the folder as it changes
Icon toolbars you show or hide one by one (Editing, Code, View, Panels), and a status bar you can hide
16 text encodings, with Reopen with Encoding, and Compare Two Files as a diff
Session restore that keeps even your unsaved text
Tabs that mark unsaved changes and can be dragged to reorder. Match macOS, Light or Dark appearance
items.alt: The jplus2 editor with the explorer sidebar and a Python file.

items.title: Type a few letters. You are there.
items.text: Press ⌘P and type. jplus2 finds a file from a few of its letters in order, so mpy finds src/main.py, and name:42 opens it at line 42.
bullets: In the same panel, @ lists the symbols of the file, : goes to a line and # finds text
The Command Palette (⇧⌘P) runs any menu command by name, and shows where it lives and its shortcut
A minimap of the whole file beside the editor: click or drag on it to scroll
items.alt: The Command Palette listing the Sort Lines commands after typing “sort lines”.

items.title: It knows your code.
items.text: Completion as you type, parameter hints, descriptions when the pointer rests on a name, and marks under errors and warnings.
bullets: C, C++, Objective-C and Swift work at once, with the language servers that come with Xcode
Python works with no server at all: jplus2 reads your file and your installed modules
Go, Rust, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, Lua and more are used when their servers are on your Mac
items.alt: A completion list showing the members of a Python object.

items.title: Press F5. In any language.
items.text: Compile and Run work for every language in the menu. The output appears under your code, and after an error the caret jumps to the line the compiler names.
bullets: A Python debugger with breakpoints, stepping, the variables of the frame and an expression field
Built-in checks for JSON, XML, YAML, TOML, HTML, CSS and more
Manage Compilers shows what is installed and downloads what is missing with Homebrew, npm or pip

A real integrated terminal (⌃`): your own shell, with vim, Python's REPL and Control-C working, and several terminals in tabs. Configure Commands replaces a language's build and run commands with yours
Find in Folder (⇧⌘F) searches every text file under a folder in the background, with file filters, whole word and regular expressions
Scripts: automate edits with your own JavaScript on the open document. A script has no network, file or shell access, and each run is one undo step
items.alt: The Python debugger paused on a line, with the variables listed beside the output.

items.title: Databricks and Snowflake, right next to your code.
items.text: Save a Databricks or Snowflake connection once, then press ⌘↩ in a SQL tab. The results arrive in a grid you can copy or export as CSV. They connect through their own SQL APIs, so there is no client tool to install.
bullets: Databricks on Azure, AWS and GCP
Snowflake
Azure SQL, SQL Server and Synapse
PostgreSQL (including Azure Database for PostgreSQL)
MySQL and MariaDB (including Azure Database for MySQL)
SQLite files, with nothing to install
Excel workbooks and CSV files: every sheet becomes a table
items.alt: A SQL query over an Excel workbook, with the results in a grid under the code.

items.title: From browse to merge, without leaving.
items.text: Connect your account and jplus2 lists your repositories. The status bar shows the branch, what there is to push or pull, and how many files changed.
bullets: Browse the folders and files of your repositories without cloning them
Create a pull request, and merge it with merge, squash or rebase
Clone, commit, push, pull and fetch
Publish a folder to a new repository, create a gist, or copy a link to the current line

privacy_page.title: Privacy Policy
privacy_page.description: jplus2 collects no data: no accounts, no analytics, no tracking. See what the app, this website and the Lite download do with your information.
privacy_page.intro: jplus2 is a code editor for the Mac made by Jason Leiton. It does not collect any data about you.

sections.title: What jplus2 does not do
sections.body: jplus2 has no accounts, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking. It does not send your files, your code, or any information about how you use the app to the developer or to anyone else.

sections.title: Your files
sections.body: jplus2 opens only the files and folders you choose. They stay on your Mac. To reopen your previous session, jplus2 keeps a list of those files, and a copy of unsaved text, in its own private folder on your Mac.

sections.title: jplus2 Lite
sections.body: jplus2 Lite has no network features. It never connects to the internet by itself; the Help menu only opens this website, an email message or the donation page in your own browser when you choose them.

sections.title: Services you connect
sections.body:
jplus2 talks to other services only when you set them up and ask for something:

  • Databases. If you add a database connection, your queries go directly from your Mac to the server you entered.
  • GitHub. If you connect a GitHub account, jplus2 uses it to list your repositories and show their folders and files, to create and merge pull requests, to clone, push and pull, and to create gists when you ask. Files you open from GitHub are saved as temporary copies on your Mac.
  • AI models. If you connect a model, the question you type, and the file and selection you chose to include, are sent to that model's provider (for example Anthropic) when you press Send. If you also switch on Inline Suggestions (off unless you turn it on), the code around your cursor (about 100 lines of the file you are editing) is sent to that same model each time you pause typing, to propose the next lines. That provider's own terms and privacy policy apply to what it receives.
  • MCP servers. If you add MCP servers in AI > MCP Servers… and use Agent mode, jplus2 connects to the addresses you listed (to ask which tools they offer) and, after you approve each call, sends the arguments of that call to that server. What the server returns is passed to your AI model. Those servers are run by third parties you chose, and their own terms and privacy policies apply. The list, with any token you put in it, is kept in a private file on your Mac.

Connection details are stored on your Mac, and passwords, tokens and API keys are stored in the macOS Keychain. None of this passes through the developer of jplus2.

sections.title: This website
sections.body: This website uses no cookies, no analytics and no third-party scripts. The language you pick with the EN | ES switch is remembered in your own browser and is not sent anywhere. The free jplus2 Lite installer is hosted on GitHub, which counts how many times it is downloaded; the author sees only that total. GitHub's own privacy statement applies while you download it.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new date.

sections.title: Installing jplus2
sections.body:
Open the downloaded disk image and drag jplus2 Lite to your Applications folder. jplus2 needs macOS 12 or later and runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

If macOS says it cannot check the app the first time you open it, open System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security, find the message about jplus2 Lite and press Open Anyway. The Mac App Store version does not show this message.

sections.title: jplus2 Lite or the full version?
sections.body:
jplus2 Lite is free and can be downloaded from this website. It is an editor: syntax colouring for 95 languages, tabs, find and replace, a file explorer, Go to Anything, the Command Palette and a minimap.

The full jplus2 is available on the Mac App Store. It adds IntelliSense, Compile and Run, the Python debugger, SQL, GitHub, the AI assistant and the built-in guide. You can keep both installed.

sections.title: jplus2 for iPad
sections.body: A version for the iPad is planned for the next release. It starts as a focused editor with tabs, find and replace, completion and Files support. Details may change before it is released.

sections.title: Compile or Run says a tool comes with Xcode
sections.body: jplus2 uses Apple's developer tools for C, C++, Objective-C, Swift, Python and Git. Install Xcode from the App Store, or run xcode-select --install in Terminal, then try again.

sections.title: A language has no compiler yet
sections.body: Choose Run ▸ Manage Compilers…. The list shows which compilers are installed; tick the missing ones and press Install Selected to download them with Homebrew, npm or pip.

sections.title: Running SQL
sections.body: Open Database ▸ Manage Connections… (⇧⌘D), add a connection, then press ⌘↩ in a SQL tab. Results appear under your code. PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server need their command line clients, which you can install with Homebrew.

sections.title: Debugging Python
sections.body: Click the margin next to a line to set a breakpoint, then press F6. Use the toolbar to step through the code.

sections.title: Finding files, symbols and commands
sections.body: Press ⌘P to open a file by typing a few of its letters. Inside the same panel, @ lists the symbols of the current file, : goes to a line, # searches the file's text and > (or ⇧⌘P) runs any menu command. View ▸ Show Minimap shows or hides the map of the file.

sections.title: GitHub
sections.body: Connect your account with GitHub ▸ Account…. Then GitHub ▸ Browse Repositories… (⌥⌘G) shows the folders and files of your repositories without cloning them, and lets you create or merge pull requests.

sections.title: Light or dark appearance
sections.body: Choose jplus2 ▸ Settings ▸ Appearance: Match macOS (the default), Light or Dark. The choice sets the whole app and the colours of the code.

sections.title: The Mac App Store version
sections.body: Apple requires App Store apps to run in a sandbox, so that version uses only the tools from macOS and Xcode. It cannot start a program it has just built from C, C++ or Objective-C, and it does not offer PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server connections. When a compiler needs other files in the same folder, press Allow Folder Access… in the output pane. Claude CLI cannot be started from the sandbox either, so the assistant button always opens the chat.

sections.body: Write to {email}. Please include your macOS version and what you were doing.

items.title: Tabs that remember
items.text: Open several files in tabs. When you come back, every tab is there, even text you had not saved.

items.title: Find and replace
items.text: Normal or regular-expression search, match case, whole word and Replace All, in the current tab or in every open tab.

items.title: Edit faster
items.text: Duplicate, move, join and delete lines, change case, comment, indent, bookmarks, column editing, and macros you can save by name.

items.title: Explorer, Go to File and minimap
items.text: Open a folder and see it as a tree, jump to any file from a few letters, to a symbol with @ or a line with :. The minimap shows on the iPad and on an iPhone turned sideways.

items.title: GitHub
items.text: Browse repositories, review pull requests with diffs, comment, approve and merge, and make small commits. The token stays in the Keychain.

items.title: Tables and SQL
items.text: Open CSV, Excel and SQLite files as tables you can sort and filter, and query them with SQL. The file is never changed.

items.q: What is the difference between Lite and the full version?
items.a: Lite is a free, 5.6 MB editor for everyday text and code in 95 languages. The full version, a one-time {price} purchase on the Mac App Store, adds the integrated terminal, IntelliSense, compile and run, the Python debugger, SQL on CSV, Excel and databases, GitHub and the AI agent. There is no subscription.

items.q: Does jplus2 send my code anywhere?
items.a: No. jplus2 collects no data and has no accounts or ads. Your code goes to GitHub, a database or an AI model only when you ask for it (or, for the model, while you have Inline Suggestions switched on), directly from your Mac with the account you connected.

items.q: Which AI models can I use?
items.a: Your own Claude API key, any OpenAI-compatible service, or a model running on your Mac through Ollama. The agent proposes every edit as a diff and every command in the Terminal panel, and nothing happens until you approve it.

items.q: Why does macOS warn about an unidentified developer when I open Lite?
items.a: The free Lite download is not distributed through the Mac App Store. Control-click the app, choose Open once, and macOS remembers your choice. The full version from the Mac App Store has no such warning.

items.q: How is jplus2 different from VS Code or Sublime Text?
items.a: jplus2 is built with Cocoa for macOS, not Electron, so it starts fast and stays small. SQL on CSV and Excel, GitHub and an approval-based AI agent are built in instead of coming from extensions.
